summary: Build the missing fine payment/waiver lifecycle — fines can be created but never cleared, which blocks erasure

api.summary:
Built the missing fine lifecycle. New `apps/api/src/fines/**` module (controller + service + DTOs, wired into `app.module.ts`) gives a librarian the three things the product never had: list what's owed, record a payment, and remove a charge — as a WAIVE (real debt, written off) or a VOID (raised in error), which are deliberately separate operations. Every mutation is role-guarded, `Idempotency-Key`-protected, CAS'd on `status='outstanding'`, and writes an audit row naming the actor. `amountCents` is never mutated — full settlement only, so there is no dishonest partial-payment model.

Two defects surfaced while building it and are fixed, because the feature is wrong without them:
1. **The nightly accrual sweep resurrected write-offs.** Waive a fine on a still-active overdue loan and, at 03:00, `fine-accrual.job.ts` saw no outstanding fine, recomputed the whole running total, and re-billed it. The write-off lasted until dawn.
2. **`LoansService.returnLoan` re-billed days already paid for.** It upserted the full accrued total; the ON CONFLICT target only matches an *outstanding* row, so a paid fine was invisible to it and the return opened a second charge for the same days.

Both now hold one invariant: **outstanding for a loan = total accrued − already settled (paid + waived)**.

Erasure is now reachable end to end and proved so: outstanding fine → 400 (now naming the amount, not just the count), waive → 200, erase → 201. I also added a third redaction pass in `members.service.ts`: `fine.waived`/`fine.voided` audit rows are targeted at the fine, not the member, so neither existing pass reached them — and a waiver carries the librarian's own sentence about a named person ("her card was stolen in March"). That is exactly the residue Art. 17 is about. The financial facts (amount, currency, status, dates) survive untouched.

I stepped outside the stated file ownership for `apps/api/src/jobs/fine-accrual.job.ts` + its unit spec. Flagging it explicitly: without that change the waive endpoint is a lie.
routes: GET /t/:slug/fines?status=&memberId=&loanId=&after=&limit= — any authenticated staff of the tenant, INCLUDING volunteer (no @Roles, same as every other tenant read). status ∈ outstanding|paid|waived (unknown value → 400). limit 1–100, default 25. after = cursor, pass the previous response's nextCursor.
GET /t/:slug/fines/:id — any authenticated staff incl. volunteer. 404 if the id is unknown OR belongs to another library.
POST /t/:slug/fines/:id/pay — @StaffWrite() = owner|admin|librarian (volunteer → 403). Returns 200, NOT 201. Accepts optional Idempotency-Key header. Body may be omitted entirely.
POST /t/:slug/fines/:id/waive — @Roles('owner','admin') (librarian → 403, volunteer → 403). Returns 200. Accepts Idempotency-Key. Body REQUIRED (reason).

POST /t/:slug/fines/:id/void — @Roles('owner','admin'). Returns 200. Accepts Idempotency-Key. Body REQUIRED (reason). Same status outcome as waive, different audit action and different note text — this is the 'raised in error' operation.
CHANGED — GET /t/:slug/members/:id — response gains circulation.outstandingFinesCount (integer) alongside the existing circulation.outstandingFinesCents.
CHANGED — POST /t/:slug/members/:id/erase — the 400 refusal body gains outstandingFinesCents alongside the existing outstandingFines count.

CHANGED — POST /t/:slug/loans/:id/return — response fine.amountCents is now what is being charged NOW (accrued minus already settled for that loan), not the gross accrued total. It is null when nothing new is owed.
decisions: WAIVE IS OWNER/ADMIN; PAY IS LIBRARIAN. Recording a payment is clerical — the money is already in the drawer and the library is only writing down what happened, so whoever can check a book out can take the €2.40 that comes back with it (@StaffWrite: owner/admin/librarian). Waive and void are the only calls in the product that turn money the library is owed into money it is not owed, they leave nothing behind but an audit row, and there is no undo — same reasoning that puts member erasure on owner/admin. Traded away: a one-librarian library needs an admin to write off €0.50. The escape hatch needs no code — the owner promotes that librarian to admin, and the promotion is itself recorded.

VOID IS A SEPARATE ENDPOINT FROM WAIVE, not a flag. Both land on status 'waived' because the FineStatus enum has three values and a fourth is a migration across every tenant database plus a breaking change for every consumer that switches on status — including the web agent building against this contract right now. But they are told apart by audit action (fine.waived vs fine.voided) and by the note written on the fine. A waiver says the debt was real and the library chose not to collect; a void says there was never a debt. Recording the second as the first puts a false statement about a patron's money into the record that gets read out when they dispute a charge. Traded away: a report grouping by status cannot separate them without reading the audit log.

FULL SETTLEMENT ONLY. Partial payment done honestly needs a payments ledger (one row per tender, balance derived from the sum) and there is no such table. The alternative — decrementing amountCents — would quietly rewrite what the library said the member owed, with no record that €2.00 of a €5.00 charge was ever collected. A charge the library will accept less for is a waiver of the difference, which this module already expresses honestly.

PAY TAKES AN OPTIONAL amountCents AND REFUSES A MISMATCH (409, with the current amount). Not defensive padding: the accrual sweep grows a fine every night, so the €2.40 on screen at 09:00 can be €2.90 when the member reaches the desk. Without the check the API stamps 'paid in full' on the strength of the wrong number and the difference vanishes with no record it was owed. Optional so a plain click still works, but the web should always send it.

TOUCHED apps/api/src/jobs/fine-accrual.job.ts (+ its unit spec) — OUTSIDE the stated ownership. Without it the waive endpoint is a lie: void a fine on a still-active overdue loan and the 03:00 sweep, seeing no outstanding row, recomputes the running total from scratch and re-bills it. The sweep now nets already-settled amounts off the accrued total. One grouped query per tenant rather than an IN-list keyed on overdue loans — a big library carries six figures of overdue loans, well past what belongs in a bind-parameter list.

THE RETURN PATH NOW NETS TOO (loans.service.ts). upsertOutstandingFine's ON CONFLICT target only matches an OUTSTANDING row, so a fine paid while the book was still out was invisible to it and the return opened a second charge for the same days. The return response's fine.amountCents is now the amount charged now, not the gross accrued — and the audit row carries BOTH accruedCents and chargedCents, because a row carrying only the accrued figure would look like the member was billed money they were not billed.

MARK-LOST DELIBERATELY DOES NOT NET. A replacement fee is a different charge from overdue days, and netting it would silently reduce a €20 replacement because €3 of unrelated overdue fines happened to be waived. Existing behaviour left alone.

closeStaleOutstandingFine NOW PRESERVES `reason` AND WRITES THE DISPOSITION TO `notes`. The old circ-3 path overwrote reason with its explanation, destroying the only field that says why the money was ever owed — the exact thing a member asks about when they see a waived charge. It also leaves resolvedByUserId NULL: that is the system reconciling itself during someone's return, not a person deciding to write off a debt, and stamping the returning librarian's id would make an automatic adjustment indistinguishable from their deliberate waiver in the very record used to tell them apart.

A THIRD ERASURE REDACTION PASS. fine.paid/waived/voided audit rows are targeted at the FINE, so neither of erasure's two existing passes (member-targeted, e-mail-substring) reached them — and a waiver carries free text about a named person. The pass skips already-redacted rows, which is not an optimisation: the returned count feeds `clearedSomething`, so counting a re-swept row would grow a fresh member.erased audit row on every repeat call. Covered by a test.

READS ARE OPEN TO VOLUNTEERS AND NOTHING IS PLAN-GATED. A volunteer on the desk has to be able to see that a member owes €2.40; and collecting money a member already owes must keep working on a lapsed subscription, or the library is locked out of its own cash.

resolvedAt IS DERIVED (paidAt for a payment, updatedAt for a waiver) because the schema has no waivedAt. Documented as display-only — the exact record is the audit row — with the caveat that a later erasure redacting notes/reason moves it.

Observed in the integration run's request log — the exact status codes the web will build against: POST …/fines/<id>/pay by volunteer → 403; POST …/waive by librarian → 403; POST …/waive with {} → 400; POST …/waive by owner → 200; POST …/void → 200; GET /t/finesB/fines/<A-fine-id> → 404; GET /t/finesA/fines/<id> with B's cookie → 403; POST …/members/<id>/erase → 400 then 201 after the waiver.
open_questions: PAYMENT METHOD IS NOT MODELLED. A desk wants cash/card on the record and there is no column for it; it can only go in the free-text `notes`, which a GDPR erasure nulls. If the library needs method for reconciliation, that is a schema change (a payments ledger would carry it naturally, and would also unlock partial payment). Not invented here — the web can prompt for it as a note in the meantime.

NO AD-HOC FINE ROUTE. The schema supports loanId = null (damage, replacement, a lost library card) and there is no way to raise one. Out of scope for this contract; worth its own POST /t/:slug/fines with an amount + reason, at owner/admin, before a library asks for it.

MIXED-CURRENCY TOTALS. outstandingCents sums rows regardless of each fine's own `currency`, and labels the sum with the tenant's CURRENT setting. Pre-existing in member.circulation.outstandingFinesCents; only bites a library that changed currency mid-life. A real fix is a per-currency breakdown nobody has asked for.

WAIVE VS VOID SHARE ONE STATUS. If finance ever needs to report write-offs separately from corrections without reading the audit log, that is an added FineStatus enum value — a migration across every tenant DB plus every consumer that switches on status. Deliberately not done during a parallel build.

SHOULD PAYING/WAIVING BE POSSIBLE ON AN ERASED MEMBER'S FINE? Currently yes (nothing blocks it), but it cannot arise in practice: erasure refuses while anything is outstanding, so an erased member has no outstanding fines to settle. Flagging it in case a future path erases around that check.

I MODIFIED apps/api/src/jobs/fine-accrual.job.ts AND ITS SPEC, outside the ownership you set. If another agent owns jobs/**, that is the merge conflict to expect — and the change must survive in some form, or waive/void silently reverts overnight.

web.summary:
Built the librarian-facing half of fines: a shared `<FinesPanel>` now renders on both surfaces that previously only displayed a fine and offered nothing to do about it.

**The panel** (`apps/web/components/FinesPanel.tsx`, one client component, two scopes). Member scope defaults to what is actually owed ("Οφείλει 20,40 € · 2 πρόστιμα") with a header toggle that loads the settled history for disputes; loan scope shows every fine on the loan plus what is still owed on it. Rows carry reason, the loan link + barcode, the date raised, the amount, and a status that says *when* it was settled. Load-more when the API returns a cursor.

**Pay is the row's primary button, one click from the amount it settles.** The dialog leads with the amount, names the member and the reason, says the whole amount is recorded (pointing at the write-off for anything less), and takes an optional desk note. It ALWAYS sends `amountCents`, so a screen rendered at 09:00 cannot stamp "paid in full" on a fine the sweep grew overnight — the 409 that refuses it corrects the row *and* the open dialog to the new figure, and the second click goes through with the amount really being collected (verified live).

**Write-off is deliberately not a sibling of pay.** It is a quieter, separately labelled control, shown only to owner/admin, and it opens one dialog that forces the distinction the API cares about: waive (the debt was real) vs void (raised in error, never a debt). Nothing arms until a kind is chosen and a 3–500 character reason is typed. The two land on different endpoints and different audit actions — confirmed `fine.waived` / `fine.voided` in the tenant audit log.

Every mid-task failure lands in `Modal`'s `error` slot, never a toast — a toast fired from an open dialog can be read but never clicked (frontend-05). Successes, which close the dialog, toast. Resolutions update the member's circulation totals in place from the response's recomputed summary, so the librarian sees the effect without a reload — and settled rows stay on screen carrying their new status rather than silently vanishing.

Two fixes fell out: the member page hardcoded `currency: 'EUR'` while the API returns the library's configured currency (now read from the fines summary, via one `formatMoney` helper that does the subunit division in exactly one place), and the loan page's fines table was headed by `common.actions.search` ("Search") over raw API enum values.

Volunteers see the debt and no buttons, plus a line saying why — matching the API, which answers 200 on the read and 403 on the pay.
proof: Drove the whole thing in a real browser against a real stack: audit env (Postgres :55440, Redis :6390), API on :3001, `next dev` on :3000, a Greek tenant `demo` with a member holding a €2.40 overdue fine and an €18.00 lost-book fine.

PAY: clicked Καταχώρηση πληρωμής on the €2,40 row, added the note «μετρητά, απόδειξη 118», submitted. Toast «Καταχωρήθηκε πληρωμή 2,40 €.»; the row flipped in place to «Πληρώθηκε · 25/08/2026»; the panel headline went 20,40 €/2 → 18,00 €/1 and the circulation card followed with no reload. API confirms: status paid, paidAt set, resolvedByUserId = the signed-in owner, notes «[…] payment recorded — μετρητά, απόδειξη 118», audit row `fine.paid` carrying amountCents 240.

STALE AMOUNT (the reason pay sends amountCents): opened the pay dialog on the €18,00 fine, ran `update fines set amountCents=1850` behind it, submitted. Got the red in-dialog banner «Το πρόστιμο είναι πλέον 18,50 €, όχι 18,00 € — αυξήθηκε όσο ήταν ανοιχτή η σελίδα…»; the dialog title, headline amount and the row underneath all corrected themselves to 18,50 €; the immediate resubmit succeeded («Καταχωρήθηκε πληρωμή 18,50 €.»). Nothing was ever stamped paid at the stale figure.

VOID: from the loan detail page, opened Διαγραφή οφειλής…, typed a 2-character reason and tabbed out — inline field error «Γράψτε την αιτιολογία (3–500 χαρακτήρες).» and the danger button stayed disabled; the button also stays neutral and disabled until a kind is chosen. Completed it and the audit log shows `fine.voided` with the reason, the fine's own `reason` preserved ('Lost book replacement') and `paidAt` NULL.

WAIVE: same dialog, other radio, on the English locale — audit row `fine.waived` with the reason; notes «[…] waived: Goodwill — long-standing member…»; paidAt NULL. Two distinct audit actions from one control.

VOLUNTEER: demoted the session user to `volunteer` in the control DB. API answers GET /t/demo/fines 200 and POST …/pay 403 (contract holds); the page then shows the debt, drops the Actions column entirely, and adds «Η καταχώρηση πληρωμής γίνεται από βιβλιοθηκονόμο ή διαχειριστή.» Restored to owner afterwards.

GDPR consequence closed in practice: after settling both fines the member's outstanding total reads 0,00 € with no count, which is exactly the state erasure (privacy-legal-03) requires and could never be reached before.

Also verified: the filter toggle (Όλα τα πρόστιμα → full history incl. waived/paid, then Μόνο τα εκκρεμή); an ad-hoc fine with loanId NULL renders without a loan link; mobile at 375px reflows each row into a stacked label/value card via the shared responsive layer; English locale renders throughout.

Wording fix found by looking at it: the Greek void action read «Ακύρωση προστίμου» directly beside the dialog's own «Ακύρωση» (Cancel) — a misread waiting to happen at a busy desk. Changed to «Ανάκληση» (the standard Greek term for withdrawing an act that should never have been issued); English uses "Void" rather than "Cancel" for the same reason.
Gates: `npx tsc --noEmit` in apps/web clean; `npx eslint` on all five touched/added files with --max-warnings 0 clean; `npx prettier --check` clean; `pnpm check:translations` passes (el, en).

`pnpm --filter @libriant/api exec vitest run --project integration fines` → 11 passed, so the contract this UI was built against is green as shipped. apps/api was not touched (its diff in the tree is the API agent's).
Dev-server side effects cleaned up: removed the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md that `next dev` generated in apps/web and restored apps/web/next-env.d.ts; `git status` shows only intended files.
open_questions: Both pages now call `currentSession()` to decide which buttons to draw, which is an extra /auth/me per render of two hot desk screens (the established pattern — settings, staff and six others do the same — but those are not hit between patrons). Wrapping `currentSession()` in React's `cache()` would dedupe it per request; lib/session.ts is outside my ownership, so I left it.

Money is rendered as `cents / 100` in one helper, matching the API's own `(cents / 100).toFixed(2)`. Both assume a two-decimal currency; a zero-decimal one (JPY) would render 240 as ¥2. Greek libraries bill in EUR, and a real fix needs the minor-unit exponent honoured on both sides of the wire, so the API has to move first — documented in apps/web/components/money.ts.

Fine resolutions deliberately do NOT go through the offline queue: it replays up to 18 hours later, and a payment landing the next morning (after the sweep grew the fine, or after someone waived it) is worse than one that plainly did not happen. The dialog says so explicitly. If the desk turns out to need offline payments, that is a payments-ledger conversation, not a queue-kind addition.

A waived and a voided fine both show as «Διαγράφηκε» / "Written off", because they share `status: 'waived'`. Which one it was lives in the audit log and in the fine's notes, neither of which this panel surfaces yet. A per-fine history/notes disclosure would close that; it needs no API change.

Fine `reason` is stored as English by the API ("24 day(s) overdue", "Lost book replacement") and renders untranslated inside an otherwise Greek page. Fixing it means the API emitting a code + params instead of prose — out of scope here, but it is visible in the screenshots.

verdict.reasoning:
Q1 — YES, verified over real HTTP against a booted API (port 3099), a signed-up tenant, four real staff sessions (owner/admin/librarian/volunteer created through POST /t/:slug/staff and logged in through /auth/login + /auth/complete-setup), a real member, a real book+copy, a backdated checkout and a real return that minted a EUR2.00 fine. A librarian paid it: 200, and in Postgres the four columns nothing in the product had ever written are now written — status='paid', paidAt set, resolvedByUserId = the librarian's control-plane user id, notes = '[iso] payment recorded - metrita, apodeixi 41' - with amountCents and reason untouched. Exactly one fine.paid audit row exists, actorType='user', actorId = that librarian, afterJson carrying amountCents 200 + memberId + loanId, so the money movement is attributable. The member's circulation went 200/1 to 0/0. An owner waived a second fine (paidAt stayed null, resolvedAt set, reason preserved as '6 day(s) overdue', the Greek reason written to notes) and an admin voided a third (audit action fine.voided, not fine.waived). Role separation holds in the direction that matters: volunteer pay/waive/void all 403, librarian waive 403, librarian pay 200 - and after four consecutive refusals the fine was still byte-identical in the DB (outstanding, all resolution columns NULL). A volunteer cannot write off a debt.

Q2 — YES, the whole chain runs. A member with a EUR1.50 outstanding fine: POST /members/:id/erase gives 400 'Can't erase a member with open business...' carrying outstandingFines 1 AND the new outstandingFinesCents 150. Waive the fine: 200. Erase again: 201, kept.fines 1, cleared.auditEntries 2. The fine row survives with amount/currency/status intact and reason redacted to '[erased]'; the librarian's Greek free-text waiver reason is gone from the ENTIRE audit log (0 matches on a full-table ILIKE), as is the member's name. A second erase returns alreadyErased and does NOT write a second member.erased row, so the third redaction pass did not reintroduce the clearedSomething regression it could have. I ran the same chain again through PAY instead of WAIVE and it also succeeds. privacy-legal-03 is genuinely reachable now and was not before.

Attacks all held. Same Idempotency-Key twice: second returns 200 with X-Idempotent-Replay: true, identical paidAt, one audit row. Different key on a paid fine: 409 with fineStatus. Six concurrent pays with six different keys: exactly one 200, five 409, one audit row, amountCents unchanged. Six concurrent with one key: same, no 5xx. Simultaneous pay+waive: exactly one wins, one audit row. Paying a waived fine, waiving a paid fine, voiding a waived fine: all 409. Cross-tenant: tenant A's owner holding tenant B's fine id gets 404 on GET/pay/waive against A's routes and 403 against B's routes, and B's fine is still outstanding with resolvedByUserId NULL. Anonymous: 401. Stale amount: 409 carrying currentAmountCents, fine untouched. I also verified the thing the web half depends on and nobody would notice failing: the FinesPanel reuses ONE idempotency key until a success, so I sent a stale-amount 409 with key K then immediately re-sent the corrected amount with the SAME key K - it returned a real 200, not a replayed 409 (the interceptor deletes the key on error). Same for a 400 validation failure. Without that the stale-amount UX would dead-end the desk.

What I would not ship silently: the four problems below. None of them break the two questions above; the worst is a real, reproducible financial write-off that leaves no audit row at all.

problems.issue: The new "already settled in full" branch of returnLoan calls closeStaleOutstandingFine, which flips a genuinely outstanding fine to status='waived' with resolvedByUserId NULL and writes NO audit row — a financial write-off nobody can attribute, in the one module whose whole point is that money movements are attributable.
problems.reproduction: Reproduced live. Loan 6 days overdue at 50c/day: sweep opens a 300c fine, librarian takes the 300c (status paid). Two more days pass, sweep opens a second, genuinely-owed 100c outstanding fine. The library then lowers finePerDayCents from 50 to 10 (a normal settings change). The book comes back: fineAmountCents = 8 * 10 = 80, settled = 300, so chargedCents = max(0, 80-300) = 0 and the else-branch fires. The 100c fine the member really owed is now `100:waived resolvedBy=NULL notes='closed on return — already settled in full'`, and `SELECT action FROM audit_log WHERE "targetId"='<fineId>'` returns (none). The loan.returned row says only {fineId: null, accruedCents: 80, chargedCents: 0} — nothing anywhere records that a 1.00 EUR charge was written off, or by whom. The new FinesPanel then displays it to the member as 'Diagrafike' (Written off) with a date and no explanation. The sibling call at line 551 (circ-3, overdue fines switched off) has the identical gap and silently waived a 300c fine in my second repro, but that path is PRE-EXISTING; line 540 is new code introduced by this change. Contrast with the deliberate waive/void endpoints, which cannot resolve a fine without writing fine.waived/fine.voided naming the actor.

problems.issue: upsertOutstandingFine's raw INSERT omits "createdAt", so the column falls to its DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP — which for a `timestamp(3) without time zone` column captures the database server's LOCAL wall clock and is then serialized to the client as if it were UTC. Every fine in the product is created through this statement, and the new UI is the first thing to display the value.
problems.reproduction: Reproduced live on a Postgres running Europe/Athens: `SELECT "createdAt", "updatedAt", now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'` on a freshly-minted fine returned `2026-08-25 20:24:45.912 | 2026-08-25 20:24:45.912 | 2026-08-25 17:24:45.941`, and the API served createdAt as "2026-08-25T20:24:45.912Z" against a real now() of 17:24:45Z — 180 minutes in the future. FinesPanel.tsx:417 renders exactly this as 'Katachorithike {date}' (Raised {date}), so a fine raised at 22:30 local displays as raised the following day. Worse, `resolvedAt` is derived from `updatedAt`, which Prisma writes in real UTC — so any fine raised after 21:00 local and resolved the same evening renders as having been settled BEFORE it was raised, on the money record a member is shown when they dispute a charge. Pre-existing (the INSERT is unchanged in this diff) and it will NOT bite the shipped docker-compose, whose postgres image defaults to UTC — but it bites any self-hosted install on a local-time Postgres, which is exactly the on-prem Greek library this product targets. It is only a defect now because this change made the field visible.

problems.issue: The netting invariant (outstanding = accrued minus settled) means a VOID only suppresses the days accrued up to the moment of the void. On a still-active loan the sweep re-bills every subsequent day, so a fine the librarian declared "raised in error" reappears as a fresh charge the next morning — which is the exact complaint this feature was built to end.
problems.reproduction: Reproduced live. Active loan 4 days overdue at 50c/day; sweep opens a 200c fine; owner VOIDs it with a Greek reason meaning 'wrong due date entered' (raised in error). Sweep runs again the same night: correctly does not resurrect it. Two days later (dueAt pushed back 2 days), the sweep opens a NEW 100c outstanding fine on the same loan with the same wrong due date. Because there is no route to correct dueAt on an active loan (only renew), the librarian must void again every night until the book comes back. This is the documented invariant working as designed, so it is not a code bug — but 'void = there was never a debt' and 'a new debt appears tomorrow for the same reason' cannot both be true at a desk, and the FinesPanel gives no hint that a void is only good until 03:00. Either the void should suppress future accrual for that loan, or the UI should say it doesn't.

problems.issue: `const session = await currentSession().catch(() => null); const role = session?.user.role ?? 'owner'` means any transient failure of the /auth/me call — not just the intended impersonation case — draws the pay and write-off buttons for whoever is looking, including a volunteer.
problems.reproduction: A volunteer loads the member page while the control-plane /auth/me request times out (the same 10s API_TIMEOUT_MS every other call uses). currentSession() rejects, the catch swallows it, role falls back to 'owner', and canSettle/canWriteOff both become true — so the volunteer is shown the 'Record payment' and 'Write off...' controls on a live fine. There is no privilege escalation: the API enforces @StaffWrite and @Roles('owner','admin') independently and answers 403, which I verified over HTTP. The cost is a confusing dead end at the counter (buttons that always fail) rather than the correct read-only view with its staff-only explanatory line. The impersonation case the comment cites is legitimate; conflating it with an error is what widens it. Same pattern in loans/[id]/page.tsx.
